observations.statement: PS-110 limits persisted privileged-session metadata to named identity, target, time, realm, transport, bind, and requested-versus-effective-state categories and excludes transcript and stdin by default.
PS-110 preserves operation-family tokens for Docker exec/attach, Kubernetes exec and port forwarding, remote SCM-over-SSH mutations, and browser/device authentication handoffs.

PS-111 applies no-persist and no-echo handling to named build/deploy secret-bearing surfaces, while its negative constraint also prohibits full rendering, indexing, and receipt/evidence inclusion beyond allowed redacted identity.
PS-112 permits only kind, name, namespace, and redacted status for Secret-resource rendering or evidence and places ConfigMap rendering under a distinct configurable redaction policy.
PS-112 is explicitly GUI-related because it governs user-visible disclosure or presentation, and FinalGUISpec is named as an owner hint.
PS-001 is retained as migration-lineage residue, while product coverage is assigned to fine-grained units or structural dispositions and the coarse bridge is prohibited from overriding them.
The migration account states that batch 208 did not refresh Spec Lock, generated shards, evidence bundles, auto_decisions, or plan_graph and created no executable or implementation artifacts.

PS-113 requires approval reuse to resolve through an approval_scope_key derived from a runtime identity envelope and enumerates actor, lane, package, project, run, account, tool, context, mode, requested identity, effective identity, execution_role, and approval_scope_level as inputs.

PS-113 makes lane/run/actor carryover the narrow default, gates boundary crossing on an explicit scope level, key coverage, and permission-class allowance, and scopes reject-cascade evaluation to the same key.
PS-113 names Permissions_System, Prompt_Pipeline, and human-in-the-loop as implementation surfaces and marks work-node creation false.

The following context, without being used to substantiate a core finding, identifies Goal Runtime high-risk actions as consumers of Permissions_System approval-scope, snapshot, approval-reuse, and blocked-payload rules.

candidate_findings.title: Privileged-session metadata exception and lifecycle semantics are undefined
candidate_findings.statement: Within the core window, PS-110 names allowed metadata and says transcript and stdin are not persisted by default, but it does not define whether or how that default may be overridden, who authorizes an override, required evidence, field types and nullability, retention duration, deletion timing, or access controls.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can implement materially different privileged-session retention policies, including inconsistent persistence of highly sensitive session content or metadata.

candidate_findings.title: Privileged-session applicability boundary is ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: PS-110 uses the general term session-style privileged operations while preserving five named operation families, but the core does not state whether those families are exhaustive, illustrative, or governed by a capability-based inclusion rule.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent privileged operations may receive different persistence treatment depending on tool-specific builder classification.

candidate_findings.title: Build/deploy secret classification and redacted identity are not specified
candidate_findings.statement: PS-111 enumerates secret-bearing surfaces and prohibited sinks but does not define how sensitive values are identified in mixed build args, environment files, manifests, or generated YAML, nor what fields constitute allowed redacted identity or how failures and indirect output channels are sanitized.
candidate_findings.impact: Secrets can be missed, over-redacted, or represented inconsistently across logs, errors, receipts, and tool-specific build/deploy paths.

candidate_findings.title: ConfigMap redaction has no defined safe default or policy authority
candidate_findings.statement: PS-112 delegates ConfigMap rendering to a separate configurable redaction policy because ConfigMaps may contain sensitive plaintext, but the core does not define the default policy, configuration authority, minimum mandatory masking, granularity, or fail-closed behavior for absent or invalid configuration.
candidate_findings.impact: A builder-selected or misconfigured policy could render sensitive plaintext even while Secret resources remain correctly redacted.

candidate_findings.title: GUI redaction presentation and accessibility behavior are absent
candidate_findings.statement: PS-112 is explicitly GUI-related and concerns user-visible disclosure, yet the core does not specify redacted-status vocabulary, masked placeholders, reveal affordances or prohibitions, empty/error differentiation, or accessible announcement of hidden values.
candidate_findings.impact: GUI consumers can present security state inconsistently or ambiguously, and assistive-technology users may not receive equivalent redaction truth.

candidate_findings.title: Approval scope key is a field list rather than a deterministic key contract
candidate_findings.statement: PS-113 enumerates approval_scope_key inputs but does not define input types, required versus optional fields, canonicalization, serialization, versioning, normalization of requested and effective identities, invalid-value handling, or equality and matching rules.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent consumers can derive non-equivalent keys for the same authority context or equivalent keys for distinct contexts, causing approval loss or unintended privilege reuse.

candidate_findings.title: Approval scope levels and carryover precedence are not enumerated
candidate_findings.statement: PS-113 requires an explicit approval_scope_level, scoped-key coverage, and permission-class allowance for boundary crossing but does not enumerate legal levels or boundary combinations, define permission classes that allow carryover, state conflict precedence, or specify default-deny behavior for unknown or malformed levels. It also does not resolve how package, tool, context, mode, and identity inputs constrain the stated lane/run/actor default.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can grant different cross-boundary authority from the same approval, undermining the intended narrow default and creating privilege-overreach risk.

candidate_findings.title: Reject-cascade transition, concurrency, and lifetime semantics are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: PS-113 requires reject-cascade evaluation against the same scoped key, but the core does not define cascade targets, exact versus hierarchical matching, activation and expiry, persistence, concurrent in-flight approvals, cancellation, retries, or idempotent replay behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: A rejection may fail to stop a related action, may suppress unrelated actions, or may race with an already-dispatched privileged operation.

candidate_findings.title: Validation surfaces do not provide executable security-behavior evidence
candidate_findings.statement: For PS-110 through PS-112, acceptance evidence is addressability/source-preservation oriented and validation surfaces are migration and plan-index checks; for PS-113, criteria restate the contract and validation surfaces are plan-index and ledger checks. No core acceptance oracle exercises transcript persistence, no-echo handling, redaction, key matching, cross-boundary reuse, or reject-cascade behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Plan-governance checks can pass while runtime implementations violate the security contracts, leaving no stated evidence threshold for behavioral acceptance.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: PS-110 explicitly bounds persisted metadata categories and explicitly excludes interactive transcript and stdin by default.
PS-111 explicitly covers echoing, persistence, full rendering, indexing, and receipt/evidence inclusion rather than stating only a generic secrecy goal.
PS-112 explicitly limits Secret-resource disclosure to kind, name, namespace, and redacted status and explicitly distinguishes ConfigMap handling.
PS-001's residual role, non-product status, non-override rule, and retirement of the coarse source-preserving bridge are explicit.
Cross-lane, cross-run, cross-project, and cross-account approval reuse is explicitly forbidden unless the stated scope-level, key-coverage, and permission-class gates are satisfied.
A provider session identifier alone is explicitly insufficient for approval reuse.
Reject-cascade is explicitly keyed to scoped identity rather than global, single-session, or single-lane state.
The window explicitly prevents these planning units from creating WorkNodes or implementation/source-code artifacts.

unknowns.statement: The core does not reveal whether transcript or stdin persistence can be enabled, nor the authority, evidence, retention, and deletion rules for any such exception.
The contracts and satisfaction state of PS-092, PS-102, and PS-107, on which PS-110 depends, are outside the assigned window.

The relevant contracts and satisfaction state of PS-105 and PS-108, which are dependencies of PS-111 or PS-112, are not available in the assigned core; only PS-111 is visible among PS-112's dependencies.
The classification rule for sensitive build/deploy values and the schema of allowed redacted identity are not stated.
The actual ConfigMap redaction policy, its default, and its configuration authority are not stated.
The current validity or later refresh state of governance artifacts cannot be determined from the historical batch statement; the core establishes only that batch 208 itself did not update them.
The CV-281 contract and the way it constrains PS-113 cannot be determined inside the assigned window.
The legal approval_scope_level values, permission classes that permit carryover, and matching precedence are not stated.
The exact serialization, comparison, persistence, expiry, concurrency, retry, cancellation, and replay behavior for approval_scope_key and reject-cascade state is not stated.
